speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; can you describe exactly how long the bleeding lasted and what the bruising looks like? Also, have any family members ever had similar bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of an uncle with bleeding issues and joint swelling is particularly concerning for hemophilia; have you or your father ever experienced spontaneous joint bleeding or deep muscle hematomas? Additionally, does the bleeding from your gums occur immediately after the extraction or start days later, and did the initial dental procedure involve any difficulty stopping the bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia B (Christmas Disease).

The history of joint swelling in a male relative, combined with your bleeding diathesis and lack of response to local pressure, strongly points to an X-linked coagulation factor deficiency. Given the specific combination of mucocutaneous bleeding (gums) and hemarthrosis in the family line, this is likely Factor IX deficiency.

REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, aPTT, Fibrinogen).
REQUEST TEST: Factor IX Activity Level.
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage.
